items.prompt: An ad platform receives 10k clicks/s; advertisers open a dashboard of clicks per minute per ad for the last 24 hours, refreshing every 10 s.
items.why: A fixed question (count per ad per minute) asked again and again over a firehose → count on ingest into minute buckets, so each refresh reads ~1,440 rows.

items.prompt: Analysts want to explore last quarter's raw events with filters and group-bys they decide on the fly, in seconds.
items.why: Ad-hoc dimensions can't be pre-computed. A columnar store that scans raw data fast is the answer to unpredictable queries.

items.prompt: A product page shows the same expensive 'top sellers' query to every visitor; it takes 2 s and may be up to 5 minutes stale.
items.why: One expensive query result reused many times and allowed to go stale → cache the result with a TTL. No event stream has to be folded on ingest.

items.prompt: A monitoring system must keep 10 s samples for 15 days but 1-hour data for 2 years, and long-range panels must still load in under a second.
items.why: Rollup tiers with a retention ladder: each tier is built from the one below, and the query picks the tier by range.

items.prompt: A fraud system must flag a card within 200 ms when it is used in two countries inside 10 minutes, by joining payment and login streams.
items.why: The goal is a real-time decision from windowed joins over streams, not a stored summary for later reads. Stream processing is the engine here.

items.prompt: A viral post gets 20k likes per second and its like counter row becomes a write hotspot.
items.why: Fold the increments in memory for a second and apply one +n update. Sharding can't split a single counter, and a cache doesn't absorb writes.

items.prompt: A video service shows each video's view count; it may lag by a minute, and there are 1M views/s overall.
items.why: Aggregate the view events in short windows and write batched counts. The count is a summary built on ingest, not a cached query result.
